outcome: mode of delivery (cesarean section, vaginal delivery)
maternal complications (prolonged labor, gestational diabetes, hypertensive disorders)
neonatal outcomes (low birth weight, macrosomia, NICU admissions)
cohort: A total of 40 term pregnant women were categorized into four BMI groups: underweight, normal, overweight, and obese.
finding: Both underweight and obese women face increased pregnancy-related risks, highlighting the importance of optimal pre-conception BMI.
mod_finding: Cesarean section rates increased with maternal BMI, with obese women having the highest rate (100%) and normal BMI and underweight women having the highest rates of vaginal delivery.
